decisions.reason: It extends the firm's drainage know-how into a new housing material, and the dedicated page suggests enough commitment and learning potential to keep developing it rather than withdraw quickly.

A floor-level shower drainage system is very close to the firm's existing drainage competence, so management would expect to absorb early market feedback and refine it within the current product base.
Although more design-driven than a standard technical product, it still builds directly on the firm's shower drainage knowledge and its own page indicates a meaningful commercial push.

The integrated-slope shower element is somewhat more system-oriented and thus slightly farther from core metal drainage products, but it remains close enough to existing know-how to justify continued market presence.

This product is the strongest fit with the firm's established drainage expertise, and the explicit launch statement indicates in-house development around a clear customer problem, making withdrawal unlikely.

An air-admittance valve is adjacent to drainage but less central to the firm's core product knowledge, so it carries the highest withdrawal risk even though it is still related enough to retain for now.
